title: Coordinatewise product of $\pm 1$ embeddings
statement: Let $x, y$ be binary words of length $n$, and encode each as a $\pm 1$ vector in $\bbr^n$ by sending its $i$-th bit to $-1$ when that bit is true and to $+1$ when it is false. Then for every coordinate $i$, the product of the $i$-th entries of these two embeddings equals $1$ if $x_i = y_i$ and $-1$ if $x_i \ne y_i$.
hypotheses_covered: x and y are binary words of length n
i is a coordinate index among the n positions
replaced:
For all binary words $x,y$ and every coordinate $i$,
$\mathrm{pmOne}(x)_i \cdot \mathrm{pmOne}(y)_i$ equals $1$ if $x_i = y_i$ and $-1$ otherwise.
